mainTopic: Does a change in a נערה's status after she sins change her death penalty? A dispute between תנאים
overview: The ברייתא finishes its rules about a betrothed נערה who sinned. It says where she is stoned. It also says that if she sinned and then became a בוגרת, she gets חנק instead of סקילה. The גמרא asks whether this means her punishment always changes when her body changes. It brings a contradicting ברייתא about מוציא שם רע, where she is still stoned even after growing up. Along the way, it fixes that ברייתא's wording to 'either she or her זוממין.' רבא answers that מוציא שם רע is a חידוש, so we cannot learn from it. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע pushes back: maybe the חידוש covers only a girl who has not grown up. So רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new answer. The two ברייתות follow two sides of a dispute between תנאים, seen in the משנה about a כהן גדול or king who sinned before being appointed.

steps.title: Where the guilty betrothed girl is stoned
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule on the location of the stoning. It depends on where she was when the witnesses came against her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the witnesses came after she moved to her husband's family, they stone her at the door of her father's house, as if to say: 'See what kind of child you raised.' If the witnesses came while she was still in her father's house, saying she sinned there, they stone her at the entrance of the city gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its list of rules about a betrothed נערה who sinned. Here it explains where the סקילה takes place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is caught after moving to her father-in-law's house, she is stoned at her father's door. That is a public rebuke to the parents who raised her. If she is caught while still at home, she is stoned at the city gate, which is the normal place.

keyTerms.meaning: They stone (carry out סקילה)
The entrance of her father's house
The child you raised (a rebuke to the parents)
The city gate

phrases.aramaic: סוֹקְלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: they stone her at the entrance of her father's house,
as if to say: see the child you have raised.
If witnesses came against her while she was in her father's house
saying that she committed adultery in her father's house,

phrases.aramaic: — סוֹקְלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּתַח שַׁעַר הָעִיר.
phrases.english: they stone her at the entrance of the city gate.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוקלין אותה על פתח בית אביה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Caught after leaving home: stoned at her father's door. Caught while at home: stoned at the city gate.

steps.title: She sinned, then grew up: strangulation
steps.stepSummary: If she sinned as a נערה but became a בוגרת before her trial, her punishment changes to חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she sinned and only later became a grown woman, she is judged with strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more rule: if she grew up between the sin and the trial, she gets חנק instead of סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סקילה applies only to a betrothed נערה. A grown woman who commits adultery gets חנק. This ruling means the court looks at her status at the time of judgment, not at the time of the sin. The next step questions exactly this point.

keyTerms.meaning: She sinned (literally, went bad)
She became a בוגרת, a fully grown woman past the נערה stage
Strangulation, one of the four court death penalties

phrases.english: If she sinned and afterward became fully grown,
she is judged with strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final clause of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sinned as a נערה, then became a בוגרת: חנק, not סקילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This clause is the target of the whole discussion that follows.

steps.title: Contradiction from the case of the defaming husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a change in her body always changes the death penalty. It then brings a ברייתא where she grew up and is still stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that whenever her body changes, the death penalty changes too? But a ברייתא contradicts this: a betrothed נערה sinned, and after she grew up her husband accused her (מוציא שם רע). He is not lashed and does not pay the hundred סלע, and she and her lying witnesses are brought early to be stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the rule from step 2 and turns it into a general principle. Then it attacks that principle with a different ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מוציא שם רע case she was a נערה when she sinned but a בוגרת when accused, so her body changed. Even so, she gets סקילה, the penalty of a נערה. So her status at the time of the sin seems to decide, which goes against step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (opens a challenge to a broad reading)
Her body changed (her physical status changed)
And they pointed out a contradiction
A husband who falsely accuses his new wife of sinning during betrothal
Her עדים זוממין, witnesses proven false

phrases.english: Is this to say that wherever
the body has changed, the death penalty changes?
But they pointed out a contradiction:
A betrothed young woman who committed adultery,
and after she became fully grown, he defamed her:
he is not lashed,
and he does not give one hundred sela,
she and her plotting witnesses are brought early to the place of stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: למימרא דכל היכא דאישתני גופא אישתני קטלא ורמינהי
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that she gets חנק if she grew up after sinning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In מוציא שם רע she also grew up after sinning, yet she is stoned. So a change in her body does not change her death penalty.

steps.title: Both of them stoned? Impossible
steps.stepSummary: A side question on the ברייתא's wording: she and her witnesses cannot both be stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She and her lying witnesses' are stoned? Could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops briefly to point out a problem in the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted. This sets up the fix in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses told the truth, only she is stoned. If they are proven זוממין, only they are stoned and she goes free. Both can never be stoned together, so 'she and her זוממין' cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be right)

phrases.english: She and her plotting witnesses, could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question on the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'she and her זוממין are stoned'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either she is guilty or the witnesses lied. Both cannot be executed at once.

steps.title: Fixed reading: either she or her witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording to 'either she or her זוממין.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: either she or her lying witnesses are brought early to be stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording so it makes sense. Whoever turns out guilty, she or the false witnesses, is stoned early in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'and' to 'or' solves the problem. The ruling is still about סקילה, so the contradiction from step 3 is still standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Either she or her lying witnesses
Brought early to the place of stoning

phrases.english: Rather: either she or her plotting witnesses
are brought early to the place of stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say both she and the witnesses are stoned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'either she or her זוממין,' depending on who is guilty.
steps.confusionAlert: This fix does not answer the main contradiction. It only cleans up the wording. The גמרא returns to the קשיא from step 3 in step 6.

steps.title: רבא: the defamer case is a special exception
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that מוציא שם רע is a חידוש with its own rules, so it cannot contradict the general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You are bringing proof from מוציא שם רע? That case is different, because it is a special new rule. Normally, a woman who entered the חופה but was not yet with her husband and then committed adultery gets strangulation. But in מוציא שם רע, she gets stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction from step 3. He says the מוציא שם רע case follows its own special rules, so we cannot learn general rules from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in a plain case where her status has not changed, a married woman who sinned after the חופה gets חנק. In מוציא שם רע she is married when judged and still gets סקילה. That case already breaks the normal rules, so its outcome does not undo the rule of step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
A special new rule that does not fit normal logic, so we do not learn from it
She entered the חופה (the wedding canopy)
In general, in ordinary cases

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's idea is that we do not learn general rules from a חידוש like מוציא שם רע. The next step pushes back on this answer, and step 8 gives a new one.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You are bringing up the case of a defamer?

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאנֵי מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע דְּחִידּוּשׁ הוּא,
phrases.english: A defamer is different, since it is a novel rule,
for if she entered the wedding canopy and was not yet intimate with him,
in general, and then committed adultery, it is strangulation,
whereas with a defamer, it is stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא מוציא שם רע קאמרת שאני מוציא שם רע דחידוש הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main contradiction from step 3 and resolves it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the contradicting source as a חידוש that we cannot learn from
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מוציא שם רע ruling seemed to show that the time of the sin, not her current status, decides the penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוציא שם רע is an exception with its own rules. Normally a change in status changes the penalty.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches the principle that we do not learn general rules from a חידוש.

steps.title: Maybe the Torah's special rule only covers a girl who did not grow up
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects רבא's answer. The חידוש of מוציא שם רע might only apply when her body has not changed. Once she becomes a בוגרת, the special rule may not apply at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רבא: Maybe the Torah only made its new rule where her body had not changed. Where her body did change, the Torah did not make any new rule.
steps.whatsHappening: A חכם pushes back on רבא's answer from the last step. He argues that calling מוציא שם רע a חידוש does not solve the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the stoning in the ברייתא comes from a special Torah rule, so it does not count against the general rule. רב הונא answers that a חידוש should be kept as narrow as possible. Maybe it only covers a girl who is still a נערה, and once she grows up she gets regular חנק. If so, the ברייתא, which says she is stoned even after growing up, is still a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah (literally, 'the Merciful One') made a new, unexpected rule
her body changed (she went from נערה to בוגרת)
perhaps / maybe (used to raise a possibility that weakens an argument)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rava:
Perhaps when the Merciful One made a new rule,
phrases.notes: The 'new rule' is the special stoning for a girl caught after a מוציא שם רע claim, which רבא just called a חידוש.

phrases.english: it was where her body did not change,
but where her body did change,
the Merciful One did not make a new rule!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא: דִּלְמָא כִּי חַדֵּית רַחֲמָנָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's answer that the חידוש of מוציא שם רע explains away the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חידוש may be limited to the plain case of a girl who is still a נערה. So it does not explain why a girl who already grew up is still stoned.

steps.title: A new answer: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that whether a change in status matters is argued by תנאים. He brings the משנה about a כהן גדול or king who sinned before being appointed. The first view says they bring the offering of ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Whether the change matters or not is a dispute between תנאים. As we learned: If they sinned before they were appointed, and then they were appointed, they are like ordinary people.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא's answer fell away, רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new answer. The two ברייתות simply follow two different תנאים. He starts quoting the proof from a משנה in הוריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer need to make the first ברייתא (חנק after she grows up) and the מוציא שם רע ברייתא (stoning) agree. Each one matches a different side of an older argument about whether a change in status changes the outcome. In the first view of the משנה, a person who sinned as a regular person and was later appointed still brings a regular person's offering. That means the status at the time of the sin counts.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute between תנאים
they were appointed (to be כהן גדול or king)
ordinary people (not a כהן גדול or a king)

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about קרבנות, not death penalties. The גמרא uses it only because it raises the same question: does a change in status after the sin change the result?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'it changed' and 'it did not change' is a dispute of Tannaim,
phrases.notes: He means the question of whether a change in status changes the punishment.

phrases.english: as we learned: If they sinned before they were appointed,
phrases.notes: 'They' means a כהן גדול or a king, who normally bring their own special קרבן for a mistaken sin.

phrases.english: and then they were appointed, they are like ordinary people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אִישְׁתַּנִּי וְלָא אִישְׁתַּנִּי, תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected answer with a new answer to the קשיא from step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מוציא שם רע ברייתא (stoned even after growing up) must agree with the first ברייתא (חנק after growing up), so it is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two sources follow different sides of a dispute between תנאים about whether a change in status matters, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: if they found out only after being appointed, they are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says it depends on when they found out about the sin. If they knew before being appointed, they are obligated (as ordinary people). If they found out after being appointed, they are completely exempt. This shows that for him, a change in status can wipe out the old obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: If it became known to them before they were appointed, they are obligated. If it became known after they were appointed, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with רבי שמעון's opposing view. This completes the proof that תנאים argue about whether a change in status matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the new status changes things. If the sin is discovered only after the appointment, the old obligation (a regular person's offering) is gone, and the new one does not apply to a sin from before. So he holds that a change in status matters, which fits the first ברייתא, where a girl who grew up gets חנק. The תנא קמא holds that the status at the time of the sin counts, which fits the מוציא שם רע ברייתא, where she is still stoned.

keyTerms.meaning: it became known to them (they found out they had sinned)
obligated (to bring an offering)
exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן בר יצחק solves the contradiction by splitting the sources between תנאים. רבי שמעון holds that a change in status changes the result, like the first ברייתא (חנק). The תנא קמא holds that the status at the time of the sin counts, like the מוציא שם רע ברייתא (stoning).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general question that comes up across ש״ס: do we judge a person by their status when they sinned, or by their status when the case is decided?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נוֹדַע לָהֶם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַנּוּ — חַיָּיבִים,
phrases.english: If it became known to them before they were appointed, they are obligated,
phrases.notes: Obligated to bring the offering of an ordinary person.

phrases.english: but if after they were appointed, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם נוֹדַע לָהֶם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 8 by bringing the opposing view
steps.raayaObject: That whether a change in status affects the outcome is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in הוריות: the תנא קמא versus רבי שמעון on a כהן גדול or king who sinned before being appointed
